A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoGU work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Bios, LongFact, and WildHallu, including training ablations and a human evaluation.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds ASQA evaluation, post-hoc baseline comparisons, and uncertainty-ratio experiments.

M1.justification: The atomic-claim decomposition, positive and negative revisions, sampling formulas, and SFT/DPO training objectives remain unchanged. Renaming the framework from refinement-based to decomposition-based does not alter its procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds ASQA evaluation on ambiguous factoid questions, explicitly testing generalization outside the three training datasets (Section 5.1, Table 2). This introduces a distinct out-of-domain test scenario while retaining Bios, LongFact, and WildHallu.

E2.justification: Appendices C.2-C.3 and Table 7 add P(true) and Semantic Entropy as evaluated comparators on all three original datasets with Mistral-7B. This extends comparison beyond the retained prompting and self-refinement baselines to post-hoc uncertainty estimation.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce dataset-level claim ranking and bottom-10% selection followed by GPT-4 revision for post-hoc baselines, plus SFT uncertainty ratios of 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8. Existing training and inference settings remain unchanged; UP becoming UA is a rename, not a metric change.

E4.justification: v3 adds an explicit out-of-domain generalization test on ASQA and a factuality/uncertainty-accuracy sensitivity analysis across four training uncertainty ratios (Appendix E). The latter extends beyond v1's human comparison of two ratios. Existing mismatch-data analysis, DPO-only ablation, and case study are retained.

E5.justification: Human-rating dispersion in Figure 4 and Fleiss' kappa of 0.759 remain unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty or significance testing for the model benchmark scores, and the added tables introduce no new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds ASQA results, post-hoc comparison scores, and uncertainty-ratio results in Tables 2, 7, and 9. For example, LoGU-DPO achieves ASQA factual accuracy of 84.3 for Mistral and 87.3 for Llama3. These are new evaluations; the original benchmark, generation-statistics, and DPO-only scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The claim-set definitions, factual accuracy and uncertainty metric formulas, revision sampling expressions, and training losses are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or formal derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central task, two challenges, training contribution, and factuality claims remain. v3 additionally highlights specific, targeted uncertainty expressions versus vague baseline expressions as a main finding in the abstract and introduction.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly discusses limitations of short-form QA as a knowledge probe and GPT-4o filtering of vague claims, and revises the discussion of numeric confidence. New interpretations contain overstatements: Table 7 gives Semantic Entropy higher Bios UA than LoGU-DPO, and Table 9 does not support alpha=0.2 being best on every metric.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page link and documents the post-hoc baselines' claim ranking, 10% threshold, and GPT-4 rewriting. Existing prompts, training-data counts, hyperparameters, hardware, and training times remain documented; removing the redundant hardware table row does not remove that information.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for the new baselines and ASQA, expands citations to long-form uncertainty research, and discusses follow-up work. It removes some earlier citations, including Atomic Calibration and Alignment for Honesty, while retaining the basic positioning of direct uncertainty expression against post-hoc estimation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and limitations receive localized rewrites; contribution bullets become prose, UP becomes UA, and Appendix C gains subsections. The main section order and most existing appendix text remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds three tables, relocates existing displays, updates metric headers, and removes a redundant hardware row. The five existing figures remain substantively unchanged. New presentation errors include upward arrows for incorrect-claim counts in Table 2 and an unrelated copied caption for Table 9.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the added generalization test, post-hoc comparisons, sensitivity analysis, and explicit metric limitations improve the evidence and transparency. Gains are tempered by incorrect claims of uniform superiority: Semantic Entropy exceeds LoGU-DPO on Bios UA (83.1 versus 80.7), and alpha=0.2 is not universally best. With the core method and original results unchanged, the net quality improvement is limited.
